## RA Progress Statement: Seoul–Daegu Honorific Shift Corpus  
**Reporting date:** November 9, 2026  
**Prepared for:** Winter 2027 funding review  

I am the sole RA responsible for Korean annotation on the NSF-funded Seoul–Daegu honorific shift corpus. The fall-term target is 6,000 annotated utterances. As of this report, 4,200 utterances have been completed.

### Timeline and work completed

- **September 3, 2026:** I sent Prof. Hollander the IRB amendment required to add 14 new Daegu recordings. I was not permitted to access or annotate those recordings until the amendment was signed.
- **September 12, September 24, and October 6:** I sent email reminders requesting the signature. I have retained these messages.
- **September 3–October 15:** While work on the new recordings was on hold, I recoded the existing 2,300 utterances using the revised speech-level scheme Prof. Hollander requested in August. This recoding was not part of the original project timeline and represents additional work completed during the waiting period.
- **October 15:** Prof. Hollander signed the amendment, six weeks after I initially sent it, and annotation of the new recordings could begin.
- **October 15–November 9:** I annotated approximately 1,900 utterances, averaging more than 500 per week. This exceeds the planned rate of 350 utterances per week.

At the November 6 lab meeting, my annotation was publicly described as “six weeks behind.” Without the timeline above, that description could suggest that the delay resulted from my working pace or care. The six-week delay in starting the new recordings resulted from the interval between submission and signature of the IRB amendment. Since receiving access, my output has exceeded the planned weekly rate.

### Expected completion and requested review record

The remaining 1,800 utterances are achievable at my current pace, and I expect to reach the 6,000-utterance target no later than the end of January 2027.

For the Winter 2027 review, I ask that any reference to my being “six weeks behind” either be omitted or accompanied by the full timeline above, including the September 3–October 15 signature delay and my lack of access to the recordings during that period. I also ask that the recoding of 2,300 utterances be recorded as substantive progress beyond the original work plan.
